Half the mid- and high-grade tumours passed six culture rounds, while low-grade ones reached round four in the results shared. Drug tests on the organoids varied by tissue origin and grade, the first hint of truly personal screening for this cancer family.
pmc-13398836:
Carla Figus and co-authors watch the ankle's two bones grow up together in children. Their 2026 study uses three-dimensional shape analysis on the talus and calcaneus of 23 individuals from birth to age ten, grouped into four age bands. How these partner bones integrate as walking begins had never been measured jointly in this detail.

Shape changed markedly with age in both bones, with the sharpest transitions between the one-to-three and three-to-six year groups. The pair stayed strongly integrated at every age, while micro-CT scans tracked the spongy bone inside in parallel. The work gives anatomists a growth baseline for the heel-ankle complex, useful wherever children's foot development is judged.
pmc-13399136:
Shannon S Wu and colleagues tested whether a large language model shows bias when it plays the role of an insurance reviewer, in a 2026 study. Insurers increasingly use artificial intelligence for prior authorization, the approvals needed before treatment is covered. The team used oral cavity cancer reconstruction as the test case. GPT-4o had to choose between a forearm free flap operation and a simpler skin graft.

The researchers ran 19,900 simulated cases built from one standard clinical scenario. They varied only patient age, sex, race, neighborhood income, social status, and substance use history. The model approved the free flap more often for younger, Asian, or White patients and for those from wealthier areas. Older, Black, and Hispanic patients fared worse. Adding detailed tumor information evened out many of the recommendations. The authors call for safeguards and regulation before such tools judge real coverage requests.
pmc-13399336:
Giti Esmail Nia and colleagues designed a multi-part vaccine candidate against HPV16, the virus type behind many cervical cancers, in a 2026 computational and laboratory study. Computer screening picked epitopes predicted to bind immune presentation molecules strongly. Docking simulations then measured how each construct latched onto immune receptors such as TLR2 and LOX-1. The arrangement placing gp96 first, then calreticulin, then E7 scored best. The researchers built that construct's gene in a plasmid and produced the fusion peptide in E. coli Rosetta bacteria, purifying it under native conditions. They present the expressed peptide as a promising candidate for further HPV16 vaccine development.
pmc-13400436:
Alexandra A Cordeiro and a binational team compare, in 2026, COVID-19 antibody rates in people with and without HIV during the first pandemic year in Haiti and Tanzania. Most earlier data came from wealthy countries, and results from other settings conflicted. Antibodies show who has met the virus, even without symptoms.

Across both countries, people living with HIV had lower rates of antibodies against the virus than people without HIV. In Haiti, antibody rates rose faster in the group without HIV. In Tanzania, the gap also favored the uninfected group. The findings add low-income country data to a mixed global picture and raise questions about exposure, immune response and protection in this population.
pmc-13400536:
Manar M Ellaban and colleagues survey, in 2026, mental health among international medical students at Ain Shams University in Egypt, comparing those from conflict zones with peers from calmer regions. Medical study abroad is stressful, and students from war-affected areas may carry added trauma.

Of 310 students surveyed between late 2024 and early 2025, over a third met thresholds for extremely severe depression, and even more for extremely severe anxiety. About one in five met criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder, with the complex form slightly more common still. Students from conflict regions scored worse on every measure. The authors call for trauma-informed counseling, peer support and targeted services for this high-risk group.
pmc-13400736:
Ebrahim A Ramadan and co-authors design, in 2026, a hybrid neural network that finds and outlines faults in solar panel arrays from inspection images. Faulty cells waste energy and money, so spotting them early matters. Their model blends convolutional networks, which excel at local detail, with transformer networks that read wider context.

Four image collections were used, from drone thermal views to cell-level electrical glow images with many fault classes. On the thermal set the model located faulty cells with accuracy near ninety-nine percent and solid overlap scores. On a two-class cell dataset it approached perfect detection. Performance dipped on the hardest multi-class sets but still beat comparison models, supporting use across inspection styles.
pmc-13400836:
Yuanyuan Tang and Xiaoshi Liu study, in 2026, how alliin, a garlic compound, changes cholesterol handling inside liver cells. Garlic compounds are candidate tools against the artery clogging that drives heart and brain disease. The team used a human liver cell line loaded with oxidized cholesterol to mimic a fatty, stressed state.

Crucially, alliin raised the receptor that pulls cholesterol from blood while lowering the protein that destroys that receptor, a pairing confirmed by targeted tests. The authors position alliin for further study in lipid disorders.
pmc-13400936:
Eliseo Bao, Anxo Perez and Javier Parapar improve, in 2026, how large language models assess depression from social media text, focusing on whether their reasoning can be clinically trusted. Most AI screening tools give a label with little explanation, which limits adoption in care. The team trained models to produce structured rationales aligned with the DSM-5 diagnostic manual.

A reinforcement learning method rewarding both correct symptom calls and sound reasoning beat standard fine-tuning, with relative gains over ten percent in mid-sized models. Structured rationales added further gains, especially for symptoms needing context, and pushed models to cite relevant evidence.
pmc-13401736:
Pruthwiraj Sethi, Chandra Jyoti, and Pritinanda Mishra present a 2026 case of aggressive angiomyxoma of the vulva, a rare soft-tissue tumour that posed a diagnostic puzzle. The patient, a 42-year-old woman who had given birth twice, had lived with an elongated swelling on her left labia majora for ten years.

Ultrasound suggested an ordinary fatty lipoma. Wide local excision removed the tumour, and tissue examination delivered the true diagnosis. pmc-13401936:

Twenty-nine pooled mixtures were split and incubated at five temperatures from refrigeration to 50 degrees, then measured over 28 days. The standard buffer lost significant haemoglobin from day ten at room temperature and from day three at every higher temperature. The new buffer held up better by comparison in the results that follow. Statistical modelling separated which variables, temperature, time, or buffer, drove the degradation.
pmc-13402036:

Scans showed a well-defined oval mass, 20 by 13 millimeters, near the ninth rib on the right side. A PET scan gave a low uptake value of 2.2 at its peak, a reading that argued against a fast-growing cancer but could not settle the diagnosis.

pmc-13402236:

Rebuilding with a graft is the usual route; here the team saved the native ligament instead.

A torn lateral meniscus root was repaired in the same operation. At one year his knee was stable and working well, with no major problems. The authors offer repair with augmentation as an option for this rare double avulsion pattern.
pmc-13402336:

pmc-13402436:

pmc-13402936:

pmc-13403636:

pmc-13403736:

Lab tests confirmed one drug as a strong aging driver and another as a refresher of human cells.
pmc-13404036:

pmc-13404636:

pmc-13404836:

pmc-13405036:

pmc-13405236:

pmc-13405636:

pmc-13405736:

pmc-13406136:

pmc-13407736:

pmc-13407936:

pmc-13408136:

pmc-13408336:

pmc-13409036:

pmc-13409236:

pmc-13410036:

pmc-13410536:

pmc-13411636:

pmc-13412236:

pmc-13412536:

pmc-13413236:
